raw_text:
Thanks — I'll give a 12-week progressive strength program specifically modified for a right medial meniscus repair (no jumping, no deep loaded knee flexion). Focus: full-body strength, unilateral work, hip/pull/hinge dominance, quad-friendly but avoiding deep knee flexion under load (>~90° knee flexion or deep squats), knee control, mobility, and gradual load. Three strength days per week plus 1 optional accessory/conditioning day. Include progression, warm-ups, loading guidance, tempo, sets/reps, and recovery/nutrition notes aimed at supporting return to skiing (strength, stability, endurance) without risking the repaired meniscus.

Red flags / assumptions
- Surgeon clearance: low-impact strength allowed, no jumping, no deep knee flexion under load. I’ll interpret "no deep knee flexion under load" as avoiding loaded squats past ~90° knee flexion and avoiding loaded sled back squats / deep barbell squats. Bodyweight ROM work can be used if pain-free and controlled. If pain, stop and refer to physio/MD.
- No other injuries or cardiorespiratory limits.
- Client training 3 structured strength sessions/week (Mon/Wed/Fri) + optional Thu low-impact conditioning/technique.
- Progression planned via load, set/rep adjustments, and exercise difficulty.

Format: three 4-week phases — Build base/volume (weeks 1–4), Strength + stability (weeks 5–8), Intensity and ski-specific transfer (weeks 9–12). Each week lists days/sessions and sets/reps. Warm-up, primary lifts, accessory, unilateral emphasis, knee-friendly squat variants, hinge and posterior chain emphasis, core, hip abductors/adductors, and single-leg control. Include tempo and rest ranges.

Phase A — Weeks 1–4: Base strength, movement quality, mobility, quad-friendly ROM
Goal: rebuild strength, correct asymmetries, establish tolerance. Moderate loads, higher volume, emphasis on unilateral control and timed eccentrics.

Weekly schedule (3 primary sessions + optional low-impact day)
- Day A (Monday) — Lower dominant (hinge + controlled squat)
- Day B (Wednesday) — Upper push/pull
- Day C (Friday) — Lower unilateral + glute/hip focus
- Optional Day D (Thursday) — Low-impact conditioning / mobility (bike, row, pool) 20–30 min, plus prehab

General warm-up (before every session)
- 6–8 min low-impact cardio (bike/row/elliptical)
- Dynamic warm-up: banded hip circles, glute bridges 2x10, A/B/C marches, leg swings front/back and lateral 10 each, ankle mobility, 1–2 warm-up sets for main lifts at 50–60% working weight.

Weeks 1–4 details

Week 1–2
Day A — Lower (Hinge emphasis)
1) Trap-bar deadlift (or hex bar) — 4 sets x 6–8 reps, tempo 2-0-1, rest 2–3 min. Use neutral ROM; no deep knee flexion beyond ~90°. Choose load at RPE 6–7.
2) Bulgarian split squat — 3 x 8–10 each leg (front foot elevated if needed). Keep range limited so back knee does not compress; if right leg painful, reduce range or reduce load. Tempo 3-0-1, rest 90s.
3) Romanian deadlift (single-leg RDL as progression) — 3 x 8 each leg (or 3 x 10 both legs barbell RDL), focus on hip hinge and posterior chain.
4) Glute bridge or hip thrust (double-leg) — 3 x 8–10, 2s hold at top.
5) Standing banded hip abduction — 3 x 12 each side.
6) Core: Pallof press (anti-rotation) — 3 x 10 each side.

Day B — Upper (Push/Pull)
1) Barbell bench press or dumbbell bench — 4 x 6–8, rest 2 min.
2) Seated row (cable or chest-supported) — 3 x 8–10.
3) Dumbbell incline press — 3 x 8–10.
4) Lat pulldown or pull-up progression — 3 x 6–8.
5) Face pulls — 3 x 15.
6) Core: dead bug — 3 x 10 each side.

Day C — Lower (Unilateral + knee control)
1) Reverse lunge (rear foot elevated optional) — 4 x 6–8 each leg (slow descent, controlled). Avoid deep forward knee travel on right if symptomatic.
2) Step-ups to a box that keeps knee range under ~90° — 3 x 8 each leg (choose box height so thigh is roughly parallel or higher to limit deep flexion).
3) Nordic hamstring curl progressions or hamstring curl machine — 3 x 6–8 (or 3 x 10 on machine).
4) Short-arc quad extension / isometric hold — 3 x 10 (good if physio-recommended).
5) Banded monster walks (lateral) — 3 x 20 steps.
6) Core: side plank — 3 x 30–45s each side.

Weeks 3–4 — Slight progression
- Increase main lifts load by ~5% or add 1 rep per set.
- Swap Bulgarian split squat for rear-foot elevated split with heavier load if tolerated.
- Add single-leg RDL sets (3 x 8) replacing double RDL on one session.
- Keep volume similar, rest same.

Phase B — Weeks 5–8: Strength and control
Goal: increase intensity (lower reps, higher load), increase unilateral loading and eccentric control, begin more ski-specific lateral strength and tempo work. Continue avoiding deep loaded knee flexion; maintain controlled ranges.

General warm-up includes single-leg balance drills (eyes open/closed) and banded knee control.

Weeks 5–6
Day A — Lower heavy hinge + limited squat
1) Deadlift variant (conventional or trap bar heavy) — 5 x 4–5, tempo 1-0-1, rest 2.5–3.5 min.
2) Goblet squat to box (box height so knees ~90° or shallower) — 4 x 6–8 (use goblet to control depth).
3) Single-leg Romanian deadlift (weighted) — 3 x 6–8 each leg.
4) Bulgarian split squat (heavier) — 3 x 6 each leg.
5) Cable hip abduction with load — 3 x 12 each.
6) Core: anti-extension work — 3 x 10 rollouts or ab wheel (knees if needed).

Day B — Upper heavy
1) Overhead press (barbell or dumbbell) — 4 x 6.
2) Bent-over row or chest-supported row heavy — 4 x 6–8.
3) Incline dumbbell press — 3 x 8.
4) Chin-ups or weighted pull-ups — 3 x 5–6 (or lat pulldown 3 x 8).
5) Rear delt and rotator cuff work — 3 x 12.
6) Core: farmer carries 3 x 40–60m.

Day C — Lower unilateral + lateral emphasis
1) Lateral lunge to a controlled depth (no deep flexion on right) — 4 x 6 each side.
2) Step-downs (eccentric control) off low box — 3 x 8 each leg (slow 3–4s descent).
3) Nordics / ham curls — 3 x 6–8.
4) Sled pushes/pulls (low impact, no jumping) — 4 x 20–30m (build force; keep knees safe by avoiding heavy sled back squats).
5) Glute med focused work: clamshell + banded side steps — 3 x 15 each.
6) Core: anti-rotation Pallof press progression with loaded band — 3 x 12.

Weeks 7–8 — Progress intensity
- Increase deadlift by ~5–10% or add set.
- Reduce reps on accessory where appropriate and increase weight.
- Add tempo eccentric work on lunges / step downs to improve control (3–4s eccentrics).
- Introduce short-duration low-impact single-leg cycling or ski-simulator sessions for 10–15 min as conditioning (optional).

Phase C — Weeks 9–12: Intensity + Ski-specific transfer
Goal: peak strength, power (low-impact), dynamic stability, multi-plane control for skiing. Still no jumping; use loaded fast concentric movements (low amplitude) like loaded step-ups, medicine-ball rotational throws (standing) with limited knee flexion.

Weeks 9–10
Day A — Heavy lower / rate of force production focus
1) Trap-bar deadlift or deficit deadlift (if mobility allows) — 5 x 3 heavy.
2) Split squat (front foot on ground, emphasis on drive) — 4 x 5 each leg (heavier).
3) Box step-up with drive (fast concentric, control eccentric) — 3 x 6 each leg.
4) Nordic curls / hamstring slider curls — 3 x 6–8.
5) Single-leg cable or band chops (rotational core) — 3 x 10 each side.
6) Core: heavy carries (suitcase carry) 3 x 40m.

Day B — Upper / posterior chain balance
1) Weighted pull-ups or heavy lat pulldown — 4 x 4–6.
2) Barbell or dumbbell bench press heavy — 4 x 4–6.
3) Inverted row or chest-supported row heavy — 3 x 6–8.
4) Rear-delt + upper back 3 x 12.
5) Forearm / grip work as needed.
6) Core: anti-rotation + dynamic chops 3 x 8–10.

Day C — Ski-transference / unilateral stability
1) Lateral step-ups with loaded barbell on back (shallow) or dumbbells — 4 x 6 each side (limit knee flexion depth).
2) Single-leg RDL heavy — 4 x 6 each leg.
3) Cossack squat to limited depth (no deep flexion on right) — 3 x 6 each side.
4) Sled pushes with higher load — 5 x 20–30m (strength emphasis).
5) Medicine ball rotational throws (standing, from chest, 3–5kg) — 4 x 6 each side (no high impact).
6) Core: anti-extension 3 x 10.

Weeks 11–12 — Peak strength and transition
- Week 11: Slightly reduce volume but maintain intensity. Test 3–5RM on main lifts if appropriate and symptom-free (deadlift trap-bar, single-leg RDL).
- Week 12: Deload / taper (reduce volume 40–60%, maintain intensity at lower sets) and focus on movement quality, mobility, and readiness for on-snow training.

Detailed week 11–12 outline
Week 11
Day A: Deadlift 3–5RM test (after proper warm-up) OR 4 x 3 at ~90% of prior best if testing risky. Accessory as Weeks 9–10 but 2 sets each.
Day B: Upper heavy 3–5RM work on bench/rows. Keep volume moderate.
Day C: Unilateral heavy sets 3–4 x 4–6, add longer sled pushes, more sport-specific conditioning sim (ski simulator if available) 10–15 min low impact.

Week 12 (Deload)
- Reduce sets by ~50% and weights to ~60–70% of normal for compound lifts; keep 2–3 sets x 5–6 reps. Emphasize mobility, controlled single-leg balance, and neuromuscular control. No testing. Prioritize recovery and reduce fatigue going into next phase of on-snow.

Progression and exercise substitution rules
- If pain at the repair site with any exercise: reduce ROM, lower load, or substitute with isometric or open-chain quad work (e.g., short-arc quads) as tolerated. Communicate with surgeon/physio if pain persists.
- Avoid loaded deep squats and plyometrics. Replace jumps with high-velocity but low ROM moves (fast step-ups, fast sled pushes) to develop rate of force without impact.
- Prioritize single-leg strength (RDLs, split squats, step-ups) to restore asymmetry from meniscus injury.
- Use tempo: slow eccentrics (2–4s) to build control and tendon resilience; concentric slightly faster unless max strength sets (where concentric should be controlled).

Conditioning and aerobic work
- 1–2 low-impact cardio sessions/week (20–40 min steady state cycling, rowing, elliptical) separate from strength days or after sessions if capacity allows.
- Add one short high-intensity but low-impact interval session per week if tolerated: bike or ski-erg 8–10 x 30s hard with 60–90s easy.

Mobility, prehab and recovery
- Daily short mobility: ankle dorsiflexion, hip flexor stretches (avoid aggressive loaded kneeling on right knee if sensitive), hamstring and glute mobility. Foam rolling posterior chain and quad as tolerated.
- Prehab 3×/week: banded glute work (clams, monster walks), terminal knee extensions / short arc quads if surgeon/physio cleared, single-leg balance 2–3 min total.
- Sleep: target 7–9 hours/night. Hydration and protein along recommendations below.

Nutrition guidance (general)
- Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg bodyweight/day to support strength gains and repair — spread evenly across meals (~25–40 g protein per meal).
- Calories: maintain slight caloric surplus (~+200–300 kcal/day) if client wants to gain strength/muscle; maintain if currently stable body composition. Adjust for client goals.
- Carbs: prioritize around training (pre/post) for performance and recovery — 1–3 g/kg pre-workout and after sessions as needed.
- Fats: 20–30% of calories; include anti-inflammatory sources (omega-3) and maintain micronutrients (vitamin C, zinc) for tissue repair.
- Supplements (optional): creatine monohydrate 3–5 g/day, vitamin D if low, fish oil 1–2 g EPA+DHA/day. Discuss with client and their physician.

Return-to-ski considerations and timeline
- This program aims to restore strength, single-leg control, and endurance for skiing next season. Before on-snow return, incorporate progressive sport-specific exposure:
  - Start with short easy groomed runs and lower speeds.
  - No aggressive twisting falls or high-load technical turns for initial sessions.
  - Continue on-snow progression over several days/weeks to re-acclimate.
- Coordinate with surgeon/physio re: specific restrictions and clearance for on-snow load and turning.

Example microcycle (Week 6 sample)
Monday — Day A heavy deadlift + split squats + glute bridges + core
Wednesday — Day B upper heavy + rows + posterior chain accessory
Thursday — Optional low-impact 20–30 min bike + mobility + prehab
Friday — Day C unilateral lateral work + sled + hamstrings + core
Weekend — 1 low-impact steady state cardio 30–40min or rest

Monitoring and cues
- Track pain (0–10), swelling, and function. If new swelling or persistent pain >3/10, stop and refer.
- Watch for compensations: trunk lean on single-leg tasks, excessive valgus at knee — cue hip drive and posterior shift.
- Use RPE to progress: aim for RPE 6–8 in base phase, 7–9 in strength phase. Avoid maximal testing until cleared and comfortable.

If you want:
- I can convert this into a printable week-by-week schedule with exact weights progression templates (e.g., % of 1RM) if you want to test reps or 1RMs.
- Or supply exercise substitution list (knee-friendly alternatives) or progressions for specific problematic movements.

Would you like a 12-week PDF-style printable with each session laid out day-by-day and a sample 1RM percentage progression plan?
